title: Killzone: Mercenary
subtitle: A soldier with a different employer

body: Killzone: Mercenary is Guerrilla Cambridge's PlayStation Vita first-person shooter, first released in PAL regions on 4 September 2013. Arran Danner fights for payment rather than loyalty to one side, taking contracts during events connected to the first three Killzone games. That position gives the war another viewpoint while keeping its familiar weapons, factions and hostile locations. The handheld's two analogue sticks support the movement and aiming expected of a console shooter. A campaign of individual assignments provides a compact structure for returning to the same conflict.

Successful actions earn money that can be spent on equipment, connecting the way a mission is played to the next loadout. The player can choose weapons and specialist devices suited to a particular assignment rather than accepting one fixed set throughout the campaign. Returning to a level with different objectives asks for another approach to a known space. A familiar corridor may become a place to move quietly, complete a precise task or use a newly purchased tool. Performance gives the contract another purpose after its first completion.

Guerrilla Cambridge built Mercenary as a full first-person shooter for Vita, with competitive multiplayer alongside its campaign. Touch interactions supplement the analogue controls without replacing the central business of moving, aiming and firing. Reviewers praised the handheld presentation and handling, while questioning the story and campaign length. Walter Mair composed the music. Sony closed the game's online servers in August 2022, leaving the campaign as its continuing playable core. Its importance lies in how convincingly it carried the scale and visual identity of Killzone onto the portable system.
